identityBoundary.userAccessToken: The canonical dingtalk connection. Reads only the authorizing user's or explicitly user-visible resources.
identityBoundary.enterpriseInternalApplication: A distinct organization/application identity. Its app access token and administrator-granted visibility must not be substituted for the user token.
identityBoundary.customRobot: The separate dingtalk_bot provider. It can send webhook messages and is not a data-reading identity.

evidencePolicy: Official API existence is not evidence that the current user OAuth identity, tenant entitlement, scope, or resource grant permits a call. Unsupported identities remain catalog-only.

officialSources.note: DingTalk organization application server API reference.
Audited request methods, paths, pagination fields, and x-acs-dingtalk-access-token header from the official generated TypeScript SDK.
User access-token acquisition and revocation boundary.

domains.paginationAndBounds: At most 100 users per action page; discovery reads at most 100 users and three department pages.
domains.revocation: Every invocation resolves the current encrypted credential and lease; upstream scope/resource revocation is rechecked on the next provider call.
domains.blocker: No real DingTalk test tenant lifecycle evidence is available.

domains.paginationAndBounds: Calendar discovery is one bounded page; event pages are capped at 100 and require an ISO-8601 window no longer than 31 days.
domains.authorization: The user ID is derived from /v1.0/contact/users/me. Callers cannot select another user. Calendar event reads require a discovered calendar ResourceRef.
domains.revocation: Discovery and invocation each call DingTalk with the current token. Scope, resource, OAuth, connection, and lease revocation fail on the next call.
domains.blocker: No real tenant has proven scope grant, event visibility, rate-limit behavior, or revocation.

domains.paginationAndBounds: One page per call, capped to 100 returned records; optional due-time bounds must be paired and span at most 366 days.
domains.authorization: The user ID is derived from /v1.0/contact/users/me. Detail reads require a task ResourceRef from the latest discovery.
domains.revocation: Discovery and invocation recheck upstream access; connection and lease revocation are enforced by the Control Plane.
domains.blocker: No real tenant has proven personal/organization task visibility, scope grant, rate-limit behavior, or revocation.

domains.reason: Official APIs exist, but their enterprise-application identity, resource authorization, export semantics, and tenant entitlements are not represented by the existing user OAuth credential.
domains.blocker: Requires a separately modeled internal-app credential and real tenant document/Wiki permission tests.

domains.reason: Official storage APIs exist, but download grants, attachment size, redirect, tenant entitlement, and resource ACL behavior are not proven for user OAuth.
domains.blocker: Requires internal-app modeling and bounded real-file lifecycle evidence.

domains.reason: No generally available, user-token, read-only DingTalk table contract was proven for this connection. Yida forms are tracked separately.
domains.blocker: Requires an official GA table API, permission model, schema pagination contract, and tenant entitlement.

domains.reason: Custom robots are message-send identities. General historical conversation-content reads for a user OAuth identity were not established; bot delivery is not read authorization.
domains.blocker: No compliant user-visible history API and no real legal/tenant authorization evidence.

domains.reason: Official conference/minutes APIs exist but require separately authorized application/meeting access and may depend on product entitlement.
domains.blocker: Requires entitlement, organizer/participant visibility rules, and real transcript/minutes revocation evidence.

domains.reason: Approval APIs use organization application authorization. A user OAuth success does not authorize organization approval instances.
domains.blocker: Requires explicit process/instance allowlisting, field-level redaction policy, internal-app identity, and real tenant tests.

domains.reason: Official Yida form/process reads exist, but application/form authorization and commercial entitlement are independent of the user OAuth connection.
domains.blocker: Requires explicit app/form allowlists, Yida entitlement, internal-app credentials, and real form-instance permission tests.

defaultWritePolicy.futureRequirement: Any write action must be separately owner-enabled, use a short-lived action-specific lease and idempotency key, and emit redacted audit evidence.

rateLimits.strategy: No automatic retry is performed, preventing amplification. DingTalk 429 responses propagate as provider errors for caller-controlled backoff.
rateLimits.concurrency: The shared Connection Service action policy and lease boundary apply; each action performs only its documented bounded provider calls.
